description: Raspberry Pi CM5 vision device with an OV9782 global-shutter camera.

revisions.notes: First-generation Raze boards carry no revision marker. Any board without a marker is gen1; later revisions will be provisioned with one.

rev_source.notes: Gen 1 has no revision marker, so every board reports gen1 (PD_DEVICE_REV_DEFAULT). Before the next hardware revision, provision a marker (for example a CM5 OTP customer row or a bootloader EEPROM config key), add the revision here, and ship /usr/lib/pd-device/rev-detect; a missing marker must keep meaning gen1.

serial_source.serial8: last 8 hex digits of the serial

identity.hostname_policy: Default only. Applied at boot as the transient hostname when /etc/hostname is unset or one of the stock names (localhost, localhost.localdomain, buildroot, (none)); never written to /etc. OS-tunable in /etc/pd-device/hostname.env (PD_HOSTNAME_POLICY, PD_HOSTNAME_PATTERN, PD_HOSTNAME_STOCK).

mac_rule.seed: board serial (lowercase hex, as in serial_source)
mac_rule.fallback_seed: "machine-id:" + /etc/machine-id when no serial is readable; with neither, no address is set and the kernel picks random ones. Never a fixed constant.
mac_rule.algorithm: base = 02:b0:b1:b2:b3:b4 where b0..b4 are the first 5 bytes of sha256(seed); host side = base with the last byte XOR 0x01; each interface XORs the last byte of both with its mask

usb_gadget.serial: board serial (first 16 hex digits of /etc/machine-id without one)

network.note: USB only: gadget interfaces are bridged with each other, never with Ethernet.

storage_target_evidence: The old Raze bootloader.conf uses boot_partition=/dev/mmcblk0p1 and the PhotonVision Raze cmdline uses root=/dev/mmcblk0p2: the CM5 eMMC (mmcblk0 on a CM5 with eMMC).
Raze images are written over USB with the mass-storage-gadget boot files, which expose the eMMC as a USB disk.
All current Raze boards use CM5 eMMC. A Lite (no eMMC) variant is not planned but not ruled out; it would be a new revision with its own storage_target.
instructions: Hold the boot button on the Raze.
While holding it, connect the Raze's regular USB port (the one used for flashing) to the computer running Atlas, then release the button once the device appears.
The status LED is red while the button is held with power applied. It turns green, and the fan starts, once Atlas begins the USB boot.
The Raze enumerates as 0a5c:2712 (BCM2712 boot ROM). Atlas sends the mass-storage-gadget boot files and the eMMC appears as a USB disk to write the image to.

files.notes: Bootloader image with bootconf.txt embedded. Flash as pieeprom.bin (rpiboot recovery) or pieeprom.upd (in-OS self-update).
rpi-eeprom-digest file (sha256 of the image plus timestamp), not a cryptographic signature. Use as pieeprom.sig.
The configuration embedded in the image, extracted for reference.
rpi-eeprom recovery.bin for BCM2712 from release v2025.12.08-2712, matching the bundled pieeprom. The EEPROM flashing tool rpiboot loads as the second stage. Kept in git (about 100 KB).

leds.notes: SK6812 RGBW ring per the original leds.toml; confirm on hardware if colours look wrong.

usb-power.control: kernel gpio hogs (raze-usb-power overlay), on at boot
usb-power.power_policy: udev 60-raze-usb-power.rules: power/control=on and USB2 hardware LPM off for every USB device
